_note: B25R1-018 (owner 2026-11-03, regional world reconstruction): the region's fixed geography for new worlds (overworld GEN_VERSION 4). Coordinates are overworld tiles in the village's frame (the village is the rectangle (0,0)-(119,89), its centre (60,45); x east, y south; 12 tiles a mile, settlements.json tiles_per_mile). Every entry carries `label` (CANON: stated by Morris; CANON-INFERRED: our reading of what he states; GAME EXPANSION: ours) and `src` (paragraph ids in research/corpus/paragraphs.json). Positions are an agent design (docs/design/REGION_RECONSTRUCTION_B25R1.md section c), provisional; the relationships they satisfy are listed there. Readers: Overworld (sites, roads, regions, landmarks; region worker) and the water generator (rivers, crossings, downs; water worker). Settlements and hamlets are also listed in settlements.json (their economies); `id` joins the two.

_note_objects: landmarks[].object: what stands for the landmark in the world (Overworld.landmark_places): 'site:<settlement>/<civic slot id>' (or /square), 'structure' (built by Overworld._setup_structures), 'figure' (chalk cut in the turf, `figure` rows scaled by `scale`), 'ring' (an earthwork bank, radius r); empty: not yet a world object, so not a Landmarks entry; 'hill' (a hill, its top raised when it carries `raised`). landmarks[].raised (generation 5, Overworld._setup_raised): {r} a raised top r tiles round the landmark, climbed by steps where roads cross its rim; {site, slot, margin: [west, north, east, south]} a raised top round that site slot, steps below its door. landmarks[].pending_art: art the owner is to supply before the thing can stand or look as described (no placeholder is drawn) A landmark placed by its object (site:...) stands where the settlement's plan puts it (Overworld.landmark_places); its x, y here are that place for seed 1 (generation 6), kept equal by overworld_test.
